Hi team,

Thanks for the sync today. Per our call, I’m putting the initial bootstrap checklist and environment scoping details into one thread so we have a single source of truth for the handoff between the Acme infra team, CloudOps (our delivery partner), and Redwood implementation. Attached: privstack-bootstrap-checklist.xlsx and a first-pass network topology PNG.

High level asks from Redwood:
- Confirm desired CIDR ranges for each VPC segment (control plane, inference, storage, management).
- Confirm whether ACME wants private peering to their on-prem core or Transit Gateway via the cloud provider.
- Decide on initial quotas for GPU pool nodes and whether we should provision an initial Dedicated pool (recommended: 2x A10G equiv for staging).
- Acceptance criteria for our CI/CD handoff: terraform modules must be importable and have clear variable contracts; helm charts must support a helmfile-based overlay for env-specific values; ansible playbooks limited to machine bootstrap only (no infra changes).

Proposed immediate milestones (week 0 -> week 2):
1) Day 0–2: CIDR and peering decision (ACME)
2) Day 3–5: Finalize terraform module interface and example vars file (Redwood/CloudOps)
3) Day 6–10: CI job skeleton in Acme repo and first apply in staging (CloudOps)
4) Day 11–14: Canary deployment and smoke tests (Redwood + ACME SRE)

Please review the checklist and add comments directly in the spreadsheet. I’ll update the Drive link as we iterate.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference

Vivek —

Thanks for the plan. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the topology:

1) CIDR: We want to preserve our existing onprem ranges and avoid fragmentation — proposed ranges attached in a quick table (see inline comments in your checklist).
2) Peering: We prefer Transit Gateway peering (we operate an AWS TGW) rather than direct private peering for the first phase. Can your terraform modules support TGW attachments vs VPC peering out-of-the-box or will we need an integration shim?
3) Quotas: Staging pool is fine at 2x A10G. Production sizing TBD — we’ll follow Redwood’s recommendation once we run load tests.
4) CI: We run GitHub Actions; CloudOps will be given a service principal to perform applies in a staging account. We need to confirm the IAM roles required.

Two quick asks:
- Can you provide a minimal example of the terraform module variables and outputs we should expect (so our infra team can mock the interfaces)?
- Who will own the helm values for metrics and logging endpoints (Acme or Redwood)?

Looping in our partner CloudOps to help with IAM and TGW specifics.

—Alex (on behalf of ACME infra)

Alex / team,

Quick answers and a minimal module sketch inline to unblock your infra mocks.

TGW: Our terraform module set includes an optional tgw_attachment submodule. Default behavior (v1) is to create a VPC attachment when tgw_id is not provided; if tgw_id is set it will create the aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment resource and export the route propagation outputs. That means no shim is required — set tgw_id in stage vars and the attachment will be created. We’ll add a boolean flag `create_tgw_attachment` to gate permissions in case you want to pre-create attachments manually.

IAM: For GitHub Actions-based applies, CloudOps will need an assume-role ARN with the following minimal policy scopes: ec2:* for ENIs/subnets (restricted by resource ARNs), ec2:CreateVpc/ModifyVpcAttribute only if create_vpc=true, iam:PassRole for instance profiles, and autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup for nodepool ops. We can provide a template assume-role trust policy and a minimal permissions policy in the Drive link (INFRA-1928).

Minimal terraform module interface (example - copy into your mock):
- variables.tf (example vars):
  - var: vpc_cidr (string)
  - var: environment (string)
  - var: enable_tgw_attachment (bool, default=false)
  - var: tgw_id (string, optional)
  - var: nodepool_gpu_type (string, default="A10G")
  - var: nodepool_count (number, default=2)

- outputs.tf (example outputs):
  - output: vpc_id
  - output: public_subnet_ids
  - output: private_subnet_ids
  - output: tgw_attachment_id (if created)

Helm values ownership: Redwood will own the app-level charts (metrics scraping config, sidecar exporters) and provide a values overlay template for ACME to wire to their central logging/metrics endpoints. We expect ACME to provide secrets/endpoint URLs (not the actual chart values) — we’ll keep those out of the repo and use external secret referencing (Vault/Secrets Manager).

I’m attaching a short scaffolding example to the Drive folder and will push a sample tfvars and a helm overlay to the shared repo by end of day.

Cheers,
Irene
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
